objects.description: Alias for a single pixel value in a GIF color map (palette index). Underlying type is unsigned char.
Alias for a pointer to a row of pixel indices (unsigned char*). Note: This typedef itself is already a pointer type; ptr_type here reflects a pointer to that alias.
Generic byte type used throughout the library for raw data buffers and sub-blocks.
Prefix code type used by LZW/GIF decoding internals (prefix table entries).
Signed integer type used for GIF dimensions and positions (Left, Top, Width, Height, etc.).
Represents an RGB color entry in a color map; each component is a byte.
Palette (color table) for a GIF image or screen. Holds an array of GifColorType entries allocated on the heap.
Descriptor for a single image frame in a GIF, including position, size, interlace flag, and an optional local color map.
Represents a single GIF extension sub-block with function code and data bytes stored on the heap.
In-memory representation of a decoded image/frame including descriptor, raster data, and its associated extension blocks.

objects.definition:
typedef struct GifFileType {
	GifWord SWidth, SHeight;   /* Size of virtual canvas */
	GifWord SColorResolution;  /* How many colors can we generate? */
	GifWord SBackGroundColor;  /* Background color for virtual canvas */
	GifByteType AspectByte;    /* Used to compute pixel aspect ratio */
	ColorMapObject *SColorMap; /* Global colormap, NULL if nonexistent. */
	int ImageCount;            /* Number of current image (both APIs) */
	GifImageDesc Image;        /* Current image (low-level API) */
	SavedImage *SavedImages;   /* Image sequence (high-level API) */
	int ExtensionBlockCount;   /* Count extensions past last image */
	ExtensionBlock *ExtensionBlocks; /* Extensions past last image */
	int Error;                       /* Last error condition reported */
	void *UserData;                  /* hook to attach user data (TVT) */
	void *Private;                   /* Don't mess with this! */
} GifFileType;
objects.description: Top-level GIF context for reading or writing files/streams. Holds screen descriptor, global color map, current image, decoded frames, extension blocks, and error status. Created/opened via EGifOpen*/DGifOpen* and closed with EGifCloseFile/DGifCloseFile.
Enumeration of top-level record types encountered while parsing a GIF stream.

Function pointer type for reading GIF data from an arbitrary source. Implementations should fill the buffer with up to the requested bytes and return count read or a negative/error convention per library usage.
Function pointer type for writing GIF data to an arbitrary target. Should return the count of bytes written.
GIF89a graphics control parameters for a frame: disposal method, user input flag, frame delay, and transparency index.

functions.name: EGifOpenFileName
functions.signature: GifFileType *EGifOpenFileName(const char *GifFileName, const bool GifTestExistence, int *Error);
functions.description: Open a GIF file for writing by filename. If GifTestExistence is true, the function may check whether the target exists before writing. Returns a handle to use with EGif* encoding calls; pass it to EGifCloseFile when done.
requirements: GifFileName must point to a valid, NUL-terminated path string.
If Error is non-NULL, it will receive an error code on failure.
Must call EGifCloseFile on the returned GifFileType* when finished to release resources.
The returned pointer must not be used after EGifCloseFile.
Behavior of GifTestExistence is not fully documented; details unknown.

functions.name: EGifOpenFileHandle
functions.description: Open a GIF file for writing using an existing file descriptor/handle. Returns a GifFileType* for subsequent EGif* calls.
requirements: GifFileHandle must be a valid open handle suitable for writing binary data.
If Error is non-NULL, it will receive an error code on failure.
Caller must close with EGifCloseFile; after closing, do not reuse the GifFileType*.
Ownership/closing of the underlying file handle after EGifCloseFile is not specified in this header; behavior unknown.

functions.name: EGifOpen
functions.description: Open a GIF stream for writing using a user-supplied output callback. Enables writing GIFs to arbitrary sinks (memory, custom I/O).
requirements: writeFunc must be a valid function of type int (*)(GifFileType *, const GifByteType *, int) that returns the count of bytes written.
userPtr is passed through and can be retrieved via GifFileType->UserData; exact use is up to caller.
If Error is non-NULL, it will receive an error code on failure.
Must finalize with EGifCloseFile; do not use the handle after closing.

functions.name: EGifSpew
functions.description: Write out the entire GIF image(s) associated with the given GifFileType to the opened output, then flush/finalize the stream state (but not necessarily close). Typically used in high-level API after populating SavedImages and global descriptors.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid pointer returned by an EGifOpen* function.
GifFile should have its screen descriptor, global color map, and image frames properly populated before calling (exact required fields not fully documented here; details partially unknown).
Return value indicates success (GIF_OK) or failure (GIF_ERROR).

functions.name: EGifGetGifVersion
functions.description: Return the GIF version string (e.g., "GIF87a" or "GIF89a") that will be written for this encoder instance.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle from EGifOpen*.
Returned pointer refers to static or internal storage; do not free.

functions.name: EGifCloseFile
functions.description: Close an encoder handle and release resources associated with writing. Optionally returns an error code via ErrorCode.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid handle previously returned by EGifOpen* functions.
Do not use GifFile after this call returns.
If ErrorCode is non-NULL, it will receive an error code on failure.

functions.name: EGifPutScreenDesc
functions.signature: int EGifPutScreenDesc(GifFileType *GifFile, const int GifWidth, const int GifHeight, const int GifColorRes, const int GifBackGround, const ColorMapObject *GifColorMap);
functions.description: Legacy encoder API: write the logical screen descriptor and optional global color map to the output stream.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle from EGifOpen*.
GifWidth and GifHeight should be non-negative and within GIF limits (exact bounds not specified here; details unknown).
GifColorRes is the color resolution; valid range not documented here; details unknown.
GifBackGround is an index into the global color map if provided; must be within the map’s range if a map is supplied.
If GifColorMap is non-NULL, it must point to a valid ColorMapObject.

functions.name: EGifPutImageDesc
functions.signature: int EGifPutImageDesc(GifFileType *GifFile, const int GifLeft, const int GifTop, const int GifWidth, const int GifHeight, const bool GifInterlace, const ColorMapObject *GifColorMap);
functions.description: Legacy encoder API: write an image descriptor for the next frame with optional local color map.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle with a screen descriptor already written.
GifWidth and GifHeight should be non-negative and within the logical screen bounds (exact enforcement unspecified; details unknown).
GifLeft and GifTop specify top-left position; should be non-negative.
If GifColorMap is non-NULL, it must be a valid ColorMapObject.
GifInterlace indicates interlaced image encoding.

functions.name: EGifSetGifVersion
functions.description: Select the encoder’s output version string: if gif89 is true, output GIF89a; otherwise GIF87a.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle from EGifOpen*.
Call before writing headers that commit the version (exact timing not documented; details unknown).

functions.name: EGifPutLine
functions.description: Legacy encoder API: write a scanline of pixel indices for the current image.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle and an image descriptor must have been written.
GifLine must point to at least GifLineLen bytes of pixel indices.
GifLineLen must be non-negative.
Pixel indices must be valid indices into the active color map.

functions.name: EGifPutPixel
functions.description: Legacy encoder API: write a single pixel index to the current image.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle with a current image being written.
GifPixel must be a valid index into the active color map.

functions.name: EGifPutComment
functions.description: Write a GIF Comment extension with the given NUL-terminated text.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle.
GifComment must be a valid NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: EGifPutExtensionLeader
functions.description: Begin writing a GIF Extension block by emitting its introducer with the given function code (e.g., COMMENT_EXT_FUNC_CODE, GRAPHICS_EXT_FUNC_CODE).
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle.
GifExtCode must be a valid extension function code as defined (e.g., 0xFE, 0xF9, 0x01, 0xFF).

functions.name: EGifPutExtensionBlock
functions.signature: int EGifPutExtensionBlock(GifFileType *GifFile, const int GifExtLen, const void *GifExtension);
functions.description: Write a continuation sub-block for the current Extension, providing GifExtLen bytes of data from GifExtension.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle and an extension leader must have been started.
GifExtension must point to at least GifExtLen bytes of data.
GifExtLen must be in the valid GIF sub-block range 0..255 (exact enforcement not specified here; details partially unknown).

functions.name: EGifPutExtensionTrailer
functions.description: Finish writing the current Extension block by emitting the zero-length terminator sub-block.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle and an extension must be in progress.

functions.name: EGifPutExtension
functions.signature: int EGifPutExtension(GifFileType *GifFile, const int GifExtCode, const int GifExtLen, const void *GifExtension);
functions.description: Write a complete Extension block (leader, data sub-block(s), trailer) in one call.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle.
GifExtension must point to at least GifExtLen bytes of data, or may be NULL if GifExtLen is 0.
GifExtCode must be a valid extension function code.
GifExtLen should be within GIF sub-block size rules (details partially unknown).

functions.name: EGifPutCode
functions.signature: int EGifPutCode(GifFileType *GifFile, int GifCodeSize, const GifByteType *GifCodeBlock);
functions.description: Low-level encoder API: write an LZW code block with the given initial code size and data block pointer.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle with an image being encoded.
GifCodeSize must be a positive integer representing initial LZW code size (exact valid range not specified here; details unknown).
GifCodeBlock must point to a properly formatted GIF code sub-block sequence (details unknown).

functions.name: EGifPutCodeNext
functions.description: Continue writing LZW code data by emitting the next code sub-block(s).
requirements: GifFile must be a valid encoder handle with an ongoing code stream started by EGifPutCode.
GifCodeBlock must point to a properly formatted code sub-block sequence (details unknown).

functions.name: DGifOpenFileName
functions.description: Open a GIF file for reading by filename. Returns a handle for DGif* decoding calls.
requirements: GifFileName must point to a valid, NUL-terminated path string.
If Error is non-NULL, it will receive an error code on failure.
Must call DGifCloseFile when done; do not use the handle after closing.

functions.name: DGifOpenFileHandle
functions.description: Open a GIF file for reading using an existing file descriptor/handle.
requirements: GifFileHandle must be a valid open handle suitable for reading binary data.
If Error is non-NULL, it will receive an error code on failure.
Caller must close with DGifCloseFile; do not use the handle after closing.
Ownership/closing of the underlying handle after DGifCloseFile is not specified here; behavior unknown.

functions.name: DGifSlurp
functions.description: High-level decode: read the entire GIF from the input into the in-memory structures of GifFile (screen descriptor, global color map, frames, extensions).
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle from DGifOpen*.
Sufficient memory must be available to store the decoded structures; otherwise error D_GIF_ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEM may occur.
Return value indicates GIF_OK or GIF_ERROR.

functions.name: DGifOpen
functions.description: Open a GIF stream for reading using a user-supplied input callback, enabling decoding from arbitrary sources.
requirements: readFunc must be a valid function of type int (*)(GifFileType *, GifByteType *, int) that reads up to the requested number of bytes and returns the count read.
userPtr is stored for user use (e.g., via GifFileType->UserData).
If Error is non-NULL, it will receive an error code on failure.
Must close the handle with DGifCloseFile.

functions.name: DGifCloseFile
functions.description: Close a decoder handle and release resources. Optionally returns an error code via ErrorCode.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid handle previously returned by DGifOpen* functions.
Do not use GifFile after closing.
If ErrorCode is non-NULL, it will receive an error code on failure.

functions.name: DGifGetScreenDesc
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: read the logical screen descriptor (and global color map if present) from the input stream.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle positioned before the screen descriptor.
Call only once per stream start (exact enforcement not documented; details unknown).

functions.name: DGifGetRecordType
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: get the next record type in the stream (screen descriptor, image descriptor, extension, or terminator).
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle.
GifType must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the record type.

functions.name: DGifGetImageHeader
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: consume the image separator and read the image header prelude (position/size and local color map flag).
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle positioned at an image record.

functions.name: DGifGetImageDesc
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: read the full image descriptor, including local color map if present.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle positioned to read an image descriptor.

functions.name: DGifGetLine
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: read a scanline of pixel indices from the current image into the provided buffer.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle and an image must be in progress.
GifLine must point to at least GifLineLen bytes of writable memory.
GifLineLen must be non-negative.

functions.name: DGifGetPixel
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: get a single pixel from the current image. The exact usage is unclear from the signature; details unknown.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle with an image being read.
Semantics of the GifPixel parameter are not described; details unknown.

functions.name: DGifGetExtension
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: start reading an extension; returns the extension function code and the first data sub-block pointer.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle positioned at an extension record.
GifExtCode must be non-NULL to receive the extension function code.
GifExtension must be non-NULL to receive a pointer to the first data sub-block (may be NULL/zero-length to indicate end, details unknown).

functions.name: DGifGetExtensionNext
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: continue reading the next extension data sub-block for the current extension sequence.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle with an extension read in progress.
GifExtension must be non-NULL to receive a pointer to the next data sub-block.

functions.name: DGifGetCode
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: start reading compressed LZW code data for the current image; returns the initial code size and first code block pointer.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle positioned at image code data.
GifCodeSize must be non-NULL to receive the initial code size.
GifCodeBlock must be non-NULL to receive a pointer to the first code block.

functions.name: DGifGetCodeNext
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: get the next LZW code data sub-block in the current image’s code stream.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle with an ongoing code stream.
GifCodeBlock must be non-NULL to receive a pointer to the next block.

functions.name: DGifGetLZCodes
functions.description: Legacy decoder API: get the next LZW code value from the code stream.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle with an image code stream available.
GifCode must be non-NULL to receive the code.

functions.name: DGifGetGifVersion
functions.description: Return the GIF version string (e.g., "GIF87a" or "GIF89a") detected for the opened decoder stream.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid decoder handle.
Returned pointer refers to internal storage; do not free.

functions.name: GifErrorString
functions.description: Return a static error string describing the given GIFLIB error code (encoding or decoding).
requirements: ErrorCode should be one of the defined E_GIF_ERR_* or D_GIF_ERR_* constants, or generic values; unmapped values may return a generic message (details unknown).
Returned pointer is static; do not free.

functions.name: GifMakeMapObject
functions.description: Allocate and optionally initialize a ColorMapObject with ColorCount entries, optionally copying initial colors from ColorMap.
requirements: ColorCount must be non-negative; practical upper bounds are GIF palette limits (typically ≤256), though not specified here; details unknown.
If ColorMap is non-NULL, it must point to at least ColorCount entries.
Returned ColorMapObject must be freed with GifFreeMapObject.

functions.name: GifFreeMapObject
functions.description: Free a ColorMapObject allocated by GifMakeMapObject or otherwise owned by the caller.
requirements: Object must either be NULL or a valid pointer returned from GifMakeMapObject or compatible allocation.
Do not use Object after freeing.

functions.name: GifUnionColorMap
functions.signature: extern ColorMapObject *GifUnionColorMap(const ColorMapObject *ColorIn1, const ColorMapObject *ColorIn2, GifPixelType ColorTransIn2[]);
functions.description: Create a union/merged color map of two input color maps, optionally returning a translation table mapping indices from ColorIn2 to the union map.
requirements: ColorIn1 and ColorIn2 must be valid pointers to ColorMapObject instances.
ColorTransIn2, if non-NULL, must point to writable storage large enough to hold a mapping for all entries of ColorIn2 (exact size depends on ColorIn2->ColorCount).
Returned ColorMapObject must be freed with GifFreeMapObject.

functions.name: GifBitSize
functions.description: Return the minimum number of bits required to represent the integer n (e.g., for palette size or codes).
requirements: Input n should be non-negative; behavior for negative values is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: GifApplyTranslation
functions.signature: extern void GifApplyTranslation(SavedImage *Image, const GifPixelType Translation[]);
functions.description: Apply an index-translation table to a SavedImage’s pixel data (e.g., remapping indices after a colormap change).
requirements: Image must be a valid pointer to a SavedImage with a valid RasterBits buffer and ImageDesc dimensions set.

Translation must be a valid table mapping input indices to output indices; typical size would cover the palette (commonly 256 entries in GIF), though exact requirement is not specified here; details partially unknown.

functions.name: GifAddExtensionBlock
functions.signature: extern int GifAddExtensionBlock(int *ExtensionBlock_Count, ExtensionBlock **ExtensionBlocks, int Function, unsigned int Len, unsigned char ExtData[]);
functions.description: Append an ExtensionBlock to an array of extension blocks, growing the array and copying Len bytes from ExtData with the given function code.
requirements: ExtensionBlock_Count must be a valid pointer to the current count; it will be updated.
ExtensionBlocks must be a valid pointer to the current array pointer; it may be reallocated/updated.
Function must be a valid extension function code (e.g., COMMENT_EXT_FUNC_CODE, GRAPHICS_EXT_FUNC_CODE, etc.).
ExtData must point to at least Len bytes if Len > 0.
Len should be within GIF sub-block semantics (0..255 typical per sub-block, but this helper may store aggregated data; exact rules not specified here; details unknown).
Returns GIF_OK or GIF_ERROR.

functions.name: GifFreeExtensions
functions.description: Free an array of ExtensionBlock structures and reset the count and pointer.
requirements: ExtensionBlock_Count and ExtensionBlocks must be valid pointers to the count and array pointer previously managed by GifAddExtensionBlock or set by the library.
Safe to call with zero count or NULL array pointer.

functions.name: GifMakeSavedImage
functions.description: Allocate and append a SavedImage to a GifFileType’s SavedImages array. If CopyFrom is provided, initialize the new image as a copy.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid pointer to a GifFileType (encoder or decoder context using slurp mode).
If CopyFrom is non-NULL, it must point to a valid SavedImage whose contents can be copied.
Returned SavedImage is owned by GifFile and should be freed via GifFreeSavedImages.

functions.name: GifFreeSavedImages
functions.description: Free the SavedImages array (and associated resources) owned by a GifFileType.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid pointer whose SavedImages were previously created/populated.
After this call, GifFile->SavedImages becomes invalid; do not access it.

functions.name: DGifExtensionToGCB
functions.signature: int DGifExtensionToGCB(const size_t GifExtensionLength, const GifByteType *GifExtension, GraphicsControlBlock *GCB);
functions.description: Parse a Graphics Control Extension (GCE) byte sequence into a GraphicsControlBlock structure.
requirements: GifExtension must point to at least GifExtensionLength bytes containing a valid GCE payload.
GCB must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the parsed fields.
GifExtensionLength must reflect the extension data size; typical GCE data length is 4 bytes, not counting block sizing; exact expectations beyond that are not specified here.

functions.name: EGifGCBToExtension
functions.description: Serialize a GraphicsControlBlock into a Graphics Control Extension (GCE) byte sequence. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: GCB must be a valid pointer to a populated GraphicsControlBlock.
GifExtension must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the serialized GCE data; exact size not specified here (commonly at least 4 bytes of payload).

functions.name: DGifSavedExtensionToGCB
functions.description: Extract and parse the Graphics Control Extension associated with a specific saved image into a GraphicsControlBlock.
requirements: GifFile must be a valid pointer with SavedImages populated (e.g., via DGifSlurp).
ImageIndex must be a valid index in the range [0, GifFile->ImageCount).
GCB must be non-NULL to receive the parsed data.

functions.name: EGifGCBToSavedExtension
functions.signature: int EGifGCBToSavedExtension(const GraphicsControlBlock *GCB, GifFileType *GifFile, int ImageIndex);
functions.description: Attach or update a Graphics Control Extension for a specific SavedImage based on the provided GraphicsControlBlock.
requirements: GCB must point to a valid GraphicsControlBlock.
GifFile must be a valid pointer with a SavedImages array to modify.
ImageIndex must be a valid index in the range [0, GifFile->ImageCount).

functions.name: GifDrawText8x8
functions.signature: extern void GifDrawText8x8(SavedImage *Image, const int x, const int y, const char *legend, const int color);
functions.description: Draw a NUL-terminated ASCII text string using the built-in 8x8 font onto the SavedImage at position (x,y) with the specified palette index color.
requirements: Image must be a valid SavedImage with RasterBits allocated and ImageDesc dimensions set.
legend must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
x and y specify the upper-left origin in pixels; they should be within the image bounds to avoid clipping/overwrites (clipping behavior unspecified).
color must be a valid palette index for the image’s active color map.

functions.name: GifDrawBox
functions.signature: extern void GifDrawBox(SavedImage *Image, const int x, const int y, const int w, const int d, const int color);
functions.description: Draw a rectangular box outline at (x,y) with width w and height d using the specified palette index color.
requirements: Image must be a valid SavedImage with RasterBits allocated.
x, y, w, d should describe a rectangle within the image bounds (clipping behavior unspecified).
color must be a valid palette index.

functions.name: GifDrawRectangle
functions.signature: extern void GifDrawRectangle(SavedImage *Image, const int x, const int y, const int w, const int d, const int color);
functions.description: Draw a filled rectangle at (x,y) with width w and height d using the specified palette index color.
requirements: Image must be a valid SavedImage with RasterBits allocated.
x, y, w, d should describe a region within the image bounds (clipping/fill behavior outside bounds unspecified).
color must be a valid palette index.

functions.name: GifDrawBoxedText8x8
functions.signature: extern void GifDrawBoxedText8x8(SavedImage *Image, const int x, const int y, const char *legend, const int border, const int bg, const int fg);
functions.description: Draw a boxed label: an 8x8-font text string with a border and background at position (x,y).
requirements: Image must be a valid SavedImage with RasterBits allocated.
legend must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
x and y specify the top-left origin in pixels; should be within image bounds.
border, bg, and fg must be valid palette indices for the border color, background fill, and text color respectively.

unharnessable_functions.name: EGifOpenFileHandle
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid OS-level file descriptor for writing, which cannot be safely produced within the stub without non-portable system calls.

unharnessable_functions.name: DGifOpenFileHandle
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid OS-level file descriptor for reading, which cannot be safely produced within the stub without non-portable system calls.

data_types.description: Arbitrary binary bytes stored in a file or memory buffer with no required structure. Used when the API reads or writes raw byte streams without interpreting a particular format in the stub.
A byte buffer where each byte is treated as a palette index (0–255) referencing the active GIF color map. No header or structure, just per-pixel indices.
NUL-terminated human-readable string content. May be arbitrary UTF-8 or ASCII characters; used for comments or on-image text labels.

A byte sequence used as the payload of a GIF extension data sub-block (0–255 bytes per sub-block). Content varies by extension type (comment, application, plaintext, graphics control) and may be concatenated across multiple sub-blocks.
A sequence of bytes formatted as GIF image data sub-blocks carrying LZW-compressed codes. Begins after an initial LZW code size and continues as length-prefixed blocks.
A complete GIF byte stream beginning with a GIF87a/GIF89a header and containing a logical screen descriptor, color tables, image descriptors, image data, and optional extensions.
A mutable memory buffer provided by the caller that the function fills with bytes (e.g., decoded pixel indices). Size is specified separately by the call.
The payload bytes of a GIF Graphics Control Extension (typically 4 bytes) encoding packed fields (disposal, user input flag, transparency), delay time, and transparent color index.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for generic binary file data. Avoid embedding NUL bytes in the
# Python source itself (no literal "\x00" in string literals). Any needed
# zero byte is constructed via bytes([...]) or b"" concatenation at runtime.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _randbytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_minimal_gif(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal valid GIF file (either 87a or 89a), 1x1 pixel, 2-color GCT.
    version = b"GIF87a" if r.choice([True, False]) else b"GIF89a"
    width = 1
    height = 1
    # Packed fields for logical screen descriptor: GCT present, size 2^(N+1) with N=0 => 2 colors
    packed = 0x80 | (0 << 4) | (0 << 3) | 0  # GCT flag | color res | sort | size
    bg_index = 0
    aspect = 0
    lsd = struct.pack("<HHBBB", width, height, packed, bg_index, aspect)
    # Global Color Table: two entries (black, white)
    gct = bytes([0, 0, 0, 255, 255, 255])
    # Image Descriptor
    sep = bytes([0x2C])
    left = top = 0
    w = width
    h = height
    id_packed = 0  # no LCT, not interlaced
    img_desc = sep + struct.pack("<HHHHB", left, top, w, h, id_packed)
    # Image Data: LZW minimum code size = 2
    lzw_min = bytes([2])
    # Provide a tiny valid code stream that decodes one pixel. Use a 2-byte sub-block.
    # Sub-block structure: [len][data....][terminator]
    sub_len = bytes([2])
    sub_payload = bytes([0x4C, 0x01])
    terminator = bytes([0])
    img_data = lzw_min + sub_len + sub_payload + terminator
    trailer = bytes([0x3B])  # ';'
    return version + lsd + gct + img_desc + img_data + trailer


def _make_comment_block(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 200) -> bytes:
    # Build a valid GIF Comment Extension sequence: '!' FE [sub-blocks] 00
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    chunks.append(bytes([0x21]))  # '!'
    chunks.append(bytes([0xFE]))  # comment code
    remaining = r.randint(0, max_len)
    while remaining > 0:
        n = min(255, remaining)
        chunks.append(bytes([n]))
        chunks.append(_randbytes(r, n))
        remaining -= n
        if remaining == 0 and r.random() < 0.5 and n > 0:
            # Optional empty sub-block mid-sequence
            chunks.append(bytes([0]))
            break
    chunks.append(bytes([0]))  # terminator
    return b"".join(chunks)


def _make_app_ext_netscape_loop(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Netscape Application Extension for looping
    loops = r.randint(0, 65535)
    return bytes([0x21, 0xFF, 0x0B]) + b"NETSCAPE2.0" + bytes([0x03, 0x01]) + struct.pack("<H", loops) + bytes([0])


def _make_text_data(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Text-ish payload without literal NULs in source; all bytes are generated at runtime.
    basics = (
        b"Hello, world!\n",
        b"GIFLIB fuzz seed text\n",
        b"alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa\n",
    )
    extra = _randbytes(r, r.randint(0, 64))
    return r.choice(basics) + extra


def _make_random_blob(r: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    return _randbytes(r, size)


def _assemble_payload(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(_make_minimal_gif(r))
        if r.random() < 0.8:
            parts.append(_make_comment_block(r, max_len=128))
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(_make_app_ext_netscape_loop(r))
    else:
        parts.append(_make_comment_block(r, max_len=200))
        parts.append(_make_text_data(r))
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_make_app_ext_netscape_loop(r))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(_make_random_blob(r, r.randint(0, 128)))
    data = b"".join(parts)
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    payload = _assemble_payload(r)
    if not payload:
        payload = _randbytes(r, r.randint(1, 32))
    return payload[:MAX_SIZE]

import random
from typing import List

# This generator creates valid raw pixel index buffers (bytes 0..255).
# It targets two fuzzers:
# - EGifPutLine: consumes a scanline up to 1024 pixels; any byte values are valid indices.
# - GifApplyTranslation: uses the buffer to fill an image raster (w*h up to 32*32=1024)
#   by resizing/truncating to the raster size; any bytes are valid.
# We therefore generate between 1 and 1024 bytes of reasonably structured patterns to
# exercise different palette index distributions while remaining valid.

MAX_BYTES = 1024

_patterns = [
    # Solid fill of a single index.
    lambda rng, n: bytes([rng.randrange(256)]) * n,
    # Linear ramp 0..255 repeating.
    lambda rng, n: bytes((i % 256 for i in range(n))),
    # Reverse ramp 255..0 repeating.
    lambda rng, n: bytes(((255 - (i % 256)) for i in range(n))),
    # Checkerboard of two indices.
    lambda rng, n: bytes(((0x00, 0xFF)[i & 1] for i in range(n))),
    # Random bytes with fixed small palette (e.g., 4 colors).
    lambda rng, n: (lambda palette: bytes(palette[rng.randrange(len(palette))] for _ in range(n)))(
        [rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(4)]
    ),
    # Stripes: runs of a value with geometric run lengths.
    lambda rng, n: (lambda vals: _runs_bytes(vals, n))( [rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(8)] ),
    # Gradient within a band: choose start and step.
    lambda rng, n: (lambda start, step: bytes(((start + i*step) & 0xFF for i in range(n))))(
        rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(1, 17)
    ),
    # Low-entropy: mostly zero with occasional spikes.
    lambda rng, n: bytes((0 if rng.random() < 0.9 else rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(n))),
    # Tiled block of 16x16 palette indices pattern flattened.
    lambda rng, n: bytes((((i >> 4) ^ (i & 0xF)) & 0xFF for i in range(n))),
    # Palette sweep emphasizing powers of two and boundaries.
    lambda rng, n: bytes((_palette_sweep(i) for i in range(n))),
]

def _runs_bytes(values: List[int], n: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    idx = 0
    # Run lengths cycle: 1,2,4,8,... up to 64 then back.
    run = 1
    while len(out) < n:
        val = values[idx % len(values)]
        take = min(run, n - len(out))
        out.extend([val] * take)
        run *= 2
        if run > 64:
            run = 1
        idx += 1
    return bytes(out)

_def_sweep = [0,1,2,3,4,7,8,15,16,31,32,63,64,127,128,191,192,223,224,239,240,247,248,251,252,253,254,255]

def _palette_sweep(i: int) -> int:
    # Cycle over boundary values then fill with modulo ramp.
    if i < len(_def_sweep):
        return _def_sweep[i]
    return i % 256

def _choose_length(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias toward powers-of-two and image-like sizes, within [1, 1024].
    choices = [1,2,3,4,7,8,15,16,24,31,32,48,63,64,96,127,128,192,255,256,384,512,768,1024]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return choices[rng.randrange(len(choices))]
    return rng.randrange(1, MAX_BYTES + 1)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    n = _choose_length(rng)
    pattern = _patterns[rng.randrange(len(_patterns))]
    data = pattern(rng, n)
    # Ensure non-empty and within limit.
    if not data:
        data = b"\x00"
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_BYTES]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for ASCII/UTF-8 text inputs used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in stubs
# Targets:
# - EGifPutComment: expects a NUL-terminated C string (comment text)
# - GifDrawText8x8 / GifDrawBoxedText8x8: legend text (NUL-terminated)
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a single buffer that can be parsed by the fuzz harness to supply
#   multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls in sequence if needed.
# - Compose multiple strings separated by NUL ("\0") so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR
#   can consume the next slice as a valid C-string.
# - Include varied content to exercise paths: ASCII, UTF-8 multi-byte, long/short,
#   whitespace/newlines, punctuation, repeated patterns, and edge-like values.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Note: The harness provides additional integer parameters via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int),
# which are not sourced from this buffer here; however, including varied lengths and
# characters in our strings is sufficient for these stubs.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "Hello",
    "World",
    "GIF",
    "Comment",
    "Legend",
    "Border",
    "Background",
    "Foreground",
    "Interlace",
    "Palette",
    "ColorMap",
    "Transparency",
]

PUNCT_SETS = [
    "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{}|;:'\",.<>/?`~",
    "()[]{}<>",
    "--==++**//!!??",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "😀😃😄😁😆",
    "αβγδεζηθ",
    "日本語",
    "éüçñöß",
    "русский",
    "عربي",
]

WHITESPACE_VARIANTS = [
    " ",
    "\t",
    "\n",
    "\r\n",
    "\f\v",
]

REPEAT_PATTERNS = [
    "AB",
    "0123456789",
    "xyz",
    ".-",
]


def _rand_str_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,:;!?/()[]{}" \
        + "@#%&*+="
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))


def _rand_str_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII base with occasional Unicode chunks
    base = _rand_str_ascii(r, min_len // 2, max_len)
    # Insert 0-3 unicode samples
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
        sample = r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        pos = r.randint(0, len(base))
        base = base[:pos] + sample + base[pos:]
    return base[:max_len]


def _make_comment_variants(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    variants: List[str] = []

    # Short friendly comment
    variants.append("Generated by fuzzer")

    # ASCII random length
    variants.append(_rand_str_ascii(r, 5, 40))

    # UTF-8 with emojis/foreign scripts
    variants.append(_rand_str_utf8(r, 5, 80))

    # Multi-line
    lines = [
        "Line 1: " + _rand_str_ascii(r, 3, 12),
        "Line 2: " + r.choice(ASCII_WORDS),
        "Line 3: " + r.choice(PUNCT_SETS),
    ]
    variants.append("\n".join(lines))

    # Longish repeated pattern but within limits
    pat = r.choice(REPEAT_PATTERNS)
    variants.append((pat * r.randint(10, 80))[:500])

    # Edge-like: empty string allowed for comments
    variants.append("")

    # Whitespace heavy
    variants.append((r.choice(WHITESPACE_VARIANTS) * r.randint(5, 50)).strip("\x00"))

    # Punctuation heavy
    variants.append(r.choice(PUNCT_SETS))

    return variants


def _make_legend_variants(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    variants: List[str] = []

    # Short words for tiny overlay
    variants.append(r.choice(["OK", "Hi", "FX", "A", "Z"]))

    # Random ASCII up to a reasonable size to fit 32x32 with 8x8 font
    # Max chars that fit without wrapping horizontally: ~4 chars per line, but stubs do not clip strictly
    variants.append(_rand_str_ascii(r, 1, 16))

    # Include spaces/tabs
    variants.append(" ".join(r.sample(ASCII_WORDS, k=min(3, len(ASCII_WORDS)))))

    # UTF-8 sample legend
    variants.append(r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))

    # Newline separated two words
    variants.append("Title\nSub")

    # Empty legend (edge)
    variants.append("")

    return variants


def _assemble_null_separated(strings: List[str], max_total: int, r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Encode each as UTF-8 and NUL-terminate; stop before exceeding max_total
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace') + b"\x00"
        if len(out) + len(b) > max_total:
            break
        out += b
    # Ensure at least one NUL-terminated string
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(b"\x00")
    # Optionally add an extra randomly chosen string
    if len(out) + 2 < max_total and r.random() < 0.3:
        extra = _rand_str_utf8(r, 3, 20).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
        if len(out) + len(extra) <= max_total:
            out += extra
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool combining comment and legend variants; the fuzzer stubs will
    # consume in order: EGifPutComment uses one FUZZ_PARAM_STR; each draw function
    # uses one FUZZ_PARAM_STR for the legend. Provide multiple entries to cover calls.
    strings: List[str] = []

    # Interleave to mix types and increase variety across positions
    comments = _make_comment_variants(r)
    legends = _make_legend_variants(r)

    # Shuffle for variety but keep determinism per seed
    r.shuffle(comments)
    r.shuffle(legends)

    # Interleave a few from each
    for i in range(max(len(comments), len(legends))):
        if i < len(comments):
            strings.append(comments[i])
        if i < len(legends):
            strings.append(legends[i])

    # Ensure presence of specific interesting strings
    strings.extend([
        "GIF89a",              # recognizable token
        ";",                   # GIF terminator char alone
        "#comment",            # leading punctuation
        "© 2025",              # copyright with UTF-8
        "\tTabbed legend",     # starts with tab
        "\n",                  # lone newline
    ])

    # Assemble into a NUL-separated byte buffer
    return _assemble_null_separated(strings, MAX_TOTAL, r)

import random
from typing import List

"""
Generator for GIF LZW code sub-block streams.

Target fuzzer stubs:
- EGifPutCode: selects initial LZW code size (1..12) internally and takes a FUZZ_PARAM_STR as the first code sub-block sequence pointer.
- EGifPutCodeNext: takes subsequent FUZZ_PARAM_STR buffers for continuation blocks.

We must return a single bytes object that the harness will reuse for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and/or FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We therefore construct a valid-looking GIF image data sub-block sequence that an encoder-side low-level API might accept:
- For EGifPutCode: provide a well-formed sequence of length-prefixed sub-blocks with a terminating zero-length block, consistent with GIF spec.
- Keep size <= 512 bytes as the stub truncates to 512.
- Make blocks varied: include a range of lengths (1..255), sometimes multiple blocks, sometimes a single block, and always include a trailing 0x00 terminator to represent a complete code stream. Although the low-level APIs may accept partial streams, a valid complete sequence is most likely to exercise normal paths.
- Since the fuzzer independently chooses the initial code size (1..12), we don’t encode it here; we only provide sub-block payloads.

The payload bytes themselves don’t have to be valid LZW bitstreams for the encoder to accept them (these are write APIs). However, producing structured, varied content can trigger different internal buffering paths. We mix patterns:
- Repeating patterns
- Incrementing bytes
- Pseudo-random bytes (seeded)
- Edge-case blocks: length 1, length 255

Output: bytes suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR, already formatted as GIF data sub-blocks.
"""

MAX_TOTAL = 512  # fuzzer truncation bound; we stay within it

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _pattern_block(r: random.Random, length: int, kind: int) -> bytes:
    # kind selects different deterministic patterns to create diversity
    if kind == 0:
        # repeating single byte (including special values)
        val = r.choice([0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0xFF, r.randrange(256)])
        return bytes([val]) * length
    elif kind == 1:
        # incremental modulo 256 starting from random seed
        start = r.randrange(256)
        return bytes((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(length))
    elif kind == 2:
        # alternating two bytes
        a = r.randrange(256)
        b = r.randrange(256)
        return bytes(a if (i & 1) == 0 else b for i in range(length))
    elif kind == 3:
        # short repeating motif of size 3-8
        mlen = r.randrange(3, 9)
        motif = bytes(r.randrange(256) for _ in range(mlen))
        reps = (length + mlen - 1) // mlen
        return (motif * reps)[:length]
    else:
        # random
        return _rand_bytes(r, length)

def _make_subblocks(r: random.Random, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a series of [len][data...] sub-blocks followed by 0x00 terminator.
    # Respect 255 max per block and total size.
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    used = 0

    # Choose number of blocks (1..6), weighted to produce multiple blocks often
    n_blocks = r.choices([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], weights=[2, 4, 4, 3, 2, 1])[0]

    # Preselect some edge-case lengths to encourage interesting paths
    edge_lengths = [1, 2, 255, 64, 127, 200]

    for i in range(n_blocks):
        # Ensure room for at least length byte + terminator
        remaining = target_size - used - 1  # keep space for final 0x00 terminator
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
        # Decide block length
        if i < len(edge_lengths) and r.random() < 0.6:
            blen = min(edge_lengths[i], remaining, 255)
        else:
            # random length 1..min(remaining,255)
            blen = r.randrange(1, min(remaining, 255) + 1)
        # Pattern selection
        kind = r.randrange(5)
        data = _pattern_block(r, blen, kind)
        chunks.append(bytes([blen]) + data)
        used += 1 + blen
        if used >= target_size - 1:
            break

    # Always terminate with zero-length block
    chunks.append(b"\x00")
    return b"".join(chunks)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide overall target size within bound; bias toward medium sizes
    target = r.randrange(16, min(256, MAX_TOTAL)) if r.random() < 0.7 else r.randrange(2, MAX_TOTAL)

    # Occasionally create a single large 255 block + terminator
    if r.random() < 0.2 and target >= 257:
        payload = bytes([255]) + _rand_bytes(r, 255) + b"\x00"
        return payload[:MAX_TOTAL]

    data = _make_subblocks(r, target)

    # As an extra variation, sometimes prepend an empty blocks run (valid but no-op): [0x00] repeated
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        empties = r.randrange(1, 4)
        data = (b"\x00" * empties) + data
        # Ensure final terminator present; if multiple zeros, still valid
        if not data.endswith(b"\x00"):
            data += b"\x00"

    # Ensure within maximum size
    return data[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid GIF byte streams (GIF87a/GIF89a) with
# combinations of features to exercise decoder paths used by the provided
# fuzz stubs. It aims to keep size <= 2048 bytes (<= 4096 requirement).
# It builds small but structurally correct GIFs: single/multi-frame,
# with/without global/local color tables, interlace toggle, assorted
# extensions (comment, application, graphics control), and varied LZW code sizes.
# The output is a bytes object suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.

# Helper: build little-endian 16-bit
_def_u16 = lambda v: bytes((v & 0xFF, (v >> 8) & 0xFF))

# Minimal uncompressed LZW image data builder for GIF: we create a trivial pixel
# stream and encode it using sub-blocks. For simplicity, use a canonical pattern
# encoded as literal bytes in GIF data sub-blocks where each block is length-prefixed.
# Note: In GIF, the "image data" format is: LZW minimum code size byte, then a series
# of sub-blocks (len, data...), terminated by a zero-length block. We don't implement
# full LZW here; instead we provide precomputed compressed byte sequences for simple
# patterns for code sizes 2..8 that decoders accept. These sequences produce a short
# strip of pixels repeating a color.
# The sequences here represent: clear, literal index, end-of-information.
# For code size C, clear=2^C, eoi=2^C+1, literal indices < 2^C.
# We assemble bitstreams little-endian into bytes.

def _lzw_min_stream(min_code_size: int, literal_indices: List[int]) -> bytes:
    # Build a tiny LZW stream: [CLEAR] + literals + [EOI]
    clear = 1 << min_code_size
    eoi = clear + 1
    codes = [clear] + literal_indices + [eoi]
    code_size = min_code_size + 1
    bitbuf = 0
    bitcnt = 0
    out = bytearray()
    for code in codes:
        # write code_size bits, LSB-first
        bitbuf |= (code & ((1 << code_size) - 1)) << bitcnt
        bitcnt += code_size
        while bitcnt >= 8:
            out.append(bitbuf & 0xFF)
            bitbuf >>= 8
            bitcnt -= 8
    if bitcnt:
        out.append(bitbuf & 0xFF)
    # Split into sub-blocks (<=255 bytes each), terminated by 0x00
    res = bytearray()
    # LZW minimum code size byte
    res.append(min_code_size if min_code_size >= 2 else 2)
    i = 0
    while i < len(out):
        take = min(255, len(out) - i)
        res.append(take)
        res.extend(out[i:i+take])
        i += take
    res.append(0)
    return bytes(res)

# Build a color table of given size (entries=2^n), return bytes and (count, bits)

def _build_color_table(rng: random.Random, bits: int, base_palette: List[Tuple[int,int,int]] = None) -> bytes:
    size = 1 << bits
    table = bytearray()
    if base_palette is None:
        # Ensure entry 0 is black, 1 is white for predictable visuals
        defaults = [(0,0,0), (255,255,255)]
    else:
        defaults = base_palette
    for i in range(size):
        if defaults and i < len(defaults):
            r,g,b = defaults[i]
        else:
            r = rng.randrange(256)
            g = rng.randrange(256)
            b = rng.randrange(256)
        table += bytes((r,g,b))
    return bytes(table)

# Build a blocks sequence for a comment extension

def _ext_comment(text: str) -> bytes:
    b = text.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    out = bytearray()
    out += b"!\xFE"  # Comment extension introducer and label
    # split into 255-byte sub-blocks
    i = 0
    while i < len(b):
        take = min(255, len(b)-i)
        out.append(take)
        out += b[i:i+take]
        i += take
    out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)

# Build an application extension (e.g., NETSCAPE2.0 loop)

def _ext_netscape_loop(count: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out += b"!\xFF"  # Application Extension
    out.append(11)
    out += b"NETSCAPE2.0"
    # Data sub-block: 3 bytes: 1 (sub-block ID), loop count LSB, MSB
    out.append(3)
    out += b"\x01" + _def_u16(count)
    out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)

# Build a Graphics Control Extension

def _ext_gce(delay_cs: int, trans_index: int | None, disposal: int, user_input: bool) -> bytes:
    packed = 0
    packed |= (disposal & 0x7) << 2
    if user_input:
        packed |= 0x02
    if trans_index is not None:
        packed |= 0x01
        ti = trans_index & 0xFF
    else:
        ti = 0
    out = bytearray()
    out += b"!\xF9\x04"  # GCE, block size 4
    out.append(packed)
    out += _def_u16(max(0, min(65535, delay_cs)))
    out.append(ti)
    out.append(0)  # terminator
    return bytes(out)

# Image descriptor block

def _image_descriptor(left: int, top: int, w: int, h: int, interlace: bool, has_lct: bool, lct_bits: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out.append(0x2C)
    out += _def_u16(left)
    out += _def_u16(top)
    out += _def_u16(w)
    out += _def_u16(h)
    packed = 0
    if has_lct:
        packed |= 0x80
        packed |= (lct_bits & 0x07)
    if interlace:
        packed |= 0x40
    out.append(packed)
    return bytes(out)

# Logical Screen Descriptor

def _lsd(width: int, height: int, gct_present: bool, gct_bits: int, color_res_bits: int, bg_index: int, aspect_byte: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out += _def_u16(width)
    out += _def_u16(height)
    packed = 0
    if gct_present:
        packed |= 0x80
        packed |= (color_res_bits & 0x07) << 4
        packed |= (gct_bits & 0x07)
    else:
        packed |= (color_res_bits & 0x07) << 4
    out.append(packed)
    out.append(bg_index & 0xFF)
    out.append(aspect_byte & 0xFF)
    return bytes(out)

# Build a simple frame: optionally with GCE, LCT, and interlace

def _build_frame(rng: random.Random, canvas_w: int, canvas_h: int, palette_bits: int, have_gct: bool) -> bytes:
    # Choose image rectangle within canvas
    w = rng.randint(1, min(64, canvas_w))
    h = rng.randint(1, min(64, canvas_h))
    left = rng.randint(0, max(0, canvas_w - w))
    top = rng.randint(0, max(0, canvas_h - h))
    interlace = rng.choice([False, True])

    # Optional GCE (transparency with random index possibly within palette)
    use_gce = rng.choice([True, False])
    gce = b""
    if use_gce:
        disposal = rng.randrange(4)
        user_input = rng.choice([False, False, True])
        # transparency index present half the time; pick small index
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            trans_index = rng.randrange(1 << palette_bits)
        else:
            trans_index = None
        delay_cs = rng.choice([0, rng.randrange(1, 50), rng.randrange(50, 300)])
        gce = _ext_gce(delay_cs, trans_index, disposal, user_input)

    # Local Color Table decision
    use_lct = rng.choice([False, True])
    lct_bits = palette_bits
    lct = b""
    if use_lct:
        # sometimes choose smaller or larger (but <= 8)
        lct_bits = max(1, min(8, palette_bits + rng.choice([-1, 0, 1])))
        lct = _build_color_table(rng, lct_bits)

    # Build image descriptor
    desc = _image_descriptor(left, top, w, h, interlace, use_lct, lct_bits - 1)

    # Build trivial image data using one or two colors
    min_code_size = max(2, lct_bits if use_lct else palette_bits)
    # Fill with a small set of literal indices (repeat single color mostly)
    dominant = rng.randrange(1 << (lct_bits if use_lct else palette_bits))
    pattern = [dominant] * min(w * h, 1024)
    # Occasionally mix another color to test dictionary growth
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        alt = (dominant + 1) % (1 << (lct_bits if use_lct else palette_bits))
        for i in range(0, len(pattern), rng.randint(7, 19)):
            pattern[i] = alt
    img_data = _lzw_min_stream(min_code_size, pattern)

    return gce + desc + (lct if use_lct else b"") + img_data

# Build a complete GIF

def _build_gif(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    version = rng.choice([b"GIF87a", b"GIF89a"])
    # Canvas size
    w = rng.randint(8, 200)
    h = rng.randint(8, 200)
    # Global color table presence and size
    have_gct = rng.choice([True, True, False])
    gct_bits = rng.randint(1, 8)
    color_res_bits = max(1, min(7, gct_bits))
    bg_index = rng.randrange(1 << gct_bits) if have_gct else 0
    aspect = rng.choice([0, 49, 255])  # 0 means unspecified; others test decoder paths

    header = version
    lsd = _lsd(w, h, have_gct, gct_bits - 1, color_res_bits - 1, bg_index, aspect)
    gct = _build_color_table(rng, gct_bits) if have_gct else b""

    blocks = bytearray()

    # Optional top-level extensions before first image
    # Comment
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        comment_len = rng.randint(0, 80)
        comment_text = "Comment " + ("#" * rng.randint(0, 10))
        comment_text += " " + ''.join(chr(65 + (i % 26)) for i in range(comment_len))
        blocks += _ext_comment(comment_text)
    # Application loop extension (NETSCAPE2.0)
    if version == b"GIF89a" and rng.random() < 0.8:
        loop_count = rng.choice([0, 1, 3, 65535])
        blocks += _ext_netscape_loop(loop_count)

    # Number of frames
    frames = rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3])
    for _ in range(frames):
        blocks += _build_frame(rng, w, h, gct_bits, have_gct)

    # Trailer
    trailer = b";"

    return header + lsd + gct + bytes(blocks) + trailer


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly decide to generate a very small or moderate-size GIF
    data = _build_gif(rng)
    # Ensure within 2048 bytes to fit DGifOpen stub buffer (and <4096 requirement)
    if len(data) > 2048:
        # Regenerate with smaller canvas and fewer frames deterministically derived from seed
        rng2 = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5)
        def small() -> bytes:
            nonlocal rng2
            version = rng2.choice([b"GIF87a", b"GIF89a"])
            w = rng2.randint(8, 64)
            h = rng2.randint(8, 64)
            have_gct = True
            gct_bits = rng2.randint(1, 5)
            color_res_bits = gct_bits
            bg_index = 0
            lsd = _lsd(w, h, have_gct, gct_bits - 1, color_res_bits - 1, bg_index, 0)
            gct = _build_color_table(rng2, gct_bits, base_palette=[(0,0,0), (255,255,255)])
            frame = _build_frame(rng2, w, h, gct_bits, True)
            return version + lsd + gct + frame + b";"
        data = small()
        # Hard cap safety
        if len(data) > 2048:
            data = data[:2047] + b";"
    return data

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for valid Graphics Control Extension (GCE) payloads.
# Typical GCE payload is 4 bytes:
# Byte 0: Packed fields
#   bits 0: Transparent Color Flag
#   bits 1: User Input Flag
#   bits 2-4: Disposal Method (0..7)
#   bits 5-7: Reserved (set to 0)
# Bytes 1-2: Delay Time in hundredths of a second (little-endian)
# Byte 3: Transparent Color Index (only meaningful if bit0 set)
#
# Some encoders or APIs may accept larger buffers; the fuzzer stub clamps 4..16 bytes.
# We will primarily generate 4-byte valid payloads and sometimes extend with benign padding
# bytes (zeros or plausible extra GCE-like sequences) to exercise length handling while
# keeping the initial 4 bytes a valid GCE.

MAX_TOTAL = 16


def _le16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF))


def _build_gce(disposal: int, user_input: bool, has_transparent: bool, delay_cs: int, trans_index: int) -> bytes:
    # Clamp to valid bit widths
    disposal &= 0x7
    delay_cs &= 0xFFFF
    trans_index &= 0xFF

    packed = 0
    # disposal occupies bits 2..4
    packed |= (disposal & 0x7) << 2
    # user input flag bit1
    if user_input:
        packed |= 1 << 1
    # transparency flag bit0
    if has_transparent:
        packed |= 1

    return bytes([packed]) + _le16(delay_cs) + bytes([trans_index])


def _interesting_gce_cases() -> List[bytes]:
    cases = []
    # Minimal: no transparency, no user input, disposal unspecified (0), delay 0
    cases.append(_build_gce(0, False, False, 0, 0))
    # Transparent set with index 0
    cases.append(_build_gce(0, False, True, 0, 0))
    # Transparent set with high index
    cases.append(_build_gce(0, False, True, 0, 255))
    # Non-zero delay typical (e.g., 10 = 100ms)
    cases.append(_build_gce(0, False, False, 10, 0))
    # Long delay (2.5s)
    cases.append(_build_gce(0, False, True, 250, 1))
    # Disposal methods 1..3 (Do not dispose, background, previous)
    for disp in (1, 2, 3):
        cases.append(_build_gce(disp, False, False, 5 * disp, 0))
        cases.append(_build_gce(disp, True, True, 7 * disp, disp))
    # Max delay 0xFFFF
    cases.append(_build_gce(2, False, True, 0xFFFF, 128))
    return cases


def _pad_buffer(base: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # The stub ensures len 4..16. We sometimes add padding bytes to reach various lengths.
    target_len = rng.choice([4, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 16])
    if target_len <= len(base):
        return base[:target_len]
    # Use zero padding or plausible repeats of GCE bytes to remain benign
    padding_modes = ["zeros", "repeat_packed", "repeat_delay", "random_low"]
    mode = rng.choice(padding_modes)
    pad = bytearray()
    while len(base) + len(pad) < target_len:
        remaining = target_len - (len(base) + len(pad))
        if mode == "zeros":
            pad.extend(b"\x00" * remaining)
        elif mode == "repeat_packed":
            pad.append(base[0])
        elif mode == "repeat_delay":
            pad.extend(base[1:3])
        else:  # random_low: small values typical in extensions
            pad.append(rng.randint(0, 15))
    return base + bytes(pad[:target_len - len(base)])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    cases = _interesting_gce_cases()
    base = rng.choice(cases)

    # Occasionally synthesize a fresh combination to broaden space
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        disposal = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])
        user_input = rng.choice([False, True])
        has_trans = rng.choice([False, True])
        # Bias delay toward common UI-relevant values
        delay_choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 65535]
        delay_cs = rng.choice(delay_choices)
        trans_index = rng.randint(0, 255)
        base = _build_gce(disposal, user_input, has_trans, delay_cs, trans_index)

    # Ensure length within 4..16 as expected by the stub
    out = _pad_buffer(base, rng)
    # Safety cap
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return bytes(out)
